title: Agent identity: whose permissions does an agent use?
summary: The Conditional Access UI route starts inside a policy without explaining how to reach or create that policy, so an administrator cannot follow it from the named portal. The other required control routes and calls were verified; all sixteen cited pages were accessible in this run. Minor corrections are needed for API notes, preview qualifications and conflicting Microsoft documentation.

claims.claim: Control maker credential options is under Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: In the environment's details page, select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. ... Under Control maker credential options

claims.claim: No API for the Copilot Studio maker-credential option was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Control maker credential options API PowerShell configure-no-maker-authentication; Power Platform environment settings API maker credentials credential options sharing embedded. Read configure-no-maker-authentication; no setting-specific API appeared.

claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: An API for the embedded-maker-credentials sharing control is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials API PowerShell environment setting; Power Platform environment settings API maker credentials credential options sharing embedded. Read both cited sharing-control pages; no operation setting this control appeared.

claims.claim: The connector credential setting is at Agents > agent > Tools > tool > Overview > Details > Additional details > Credentials to use in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Select Agents and select the agent ... Go to the Tools page ... Go to the connector tool Overview page. ... Under Details > Additional details > Credentials to use, select Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: An API operation setting a connector tool's Credentials to use option is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connector tool Credentials to use maker provided credentials API; Copilot Studio connector tool YAML connectionProperties mode Maker Invoker credentials. Read advanced-connectors and configure-enduser-authentication; inventory and CLI results did not document this setter.

claims.claim: Dataverse agent users are added at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Agents > + Add agent in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: In the command bar, select Settings. ... Expand Users + permissions, and then select Agents. ... Select + Add agent from the command bar. The Add agent pane appears.

claims.claim: No API specifically documented for adding Dataverse agent users was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users add agent API systemuser Entra agent identity; Dataverse Entra agent user sync API Add-AdminPowerAppsSyncUser supported agent users. Read create-users, agent-users, add-users-to-environment and SyncUser excerpts; no agent-specific Dataverse provisioning API appeared.

claims.claim: Individual agent identities can be viewed and managed at Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities. ... Select any agent identity to view its details, including name, description, status, owners, sponsors, granted permissions, and sign-in logs.
claims.fix: For the disabling operation, extend the path to 'Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities > agent identity > Disable', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/disable-agent-identities, which is already cited.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity updates an agent identity, including its enabled state.
claims.quote: Update the properties of an agentIdentity object. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity
claims.fix: Keep the call; add to the note: 'The request body sets accountEnabled to false to disable the identity, or true to enable it.' The v1.0 property is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentidentity?view=graph-rest-1.0.

claims.claim: The route from Microsoft Entra admin center to the Conditional Access agent control is Assignments > Users, agents, or workload identities > Agents.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. ... Select New policy. ... Under Assignments, select Users, agents or workload identities.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Assignments > Users, agents, or workload identities > Agents'. The existing disable-agent-identities source supplies the entry route, and the row's agent-id source supplies the final Agents selection.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies creates the documented agent-identity policy.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies
claims.fix: Set the call to 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies'. Move the description to the note: 'The example sets conditions.clientApplications.includeAgentIdServicePrincipals to ["All"], grantControls.builtInControls to ["block"], and state to "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"; it reports rather than enforces blocking.'

claims.claim: Agent sign-in logs are under Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs.

claims.claim: The printed beta Graph GET query retrieves agent-identity service-principal sign-ins.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'
